welcome.title: This map is documents
welcome.body: Every dot you see here is one real markdown file. The whole map is a single picture of what our product is made of and how the pieces connect. Takes about 2 minutes.

nodes.title: Size and shape of the dots
nodes.body: The biggest dot is the whole product, the next size down is an area, and the small dots are individual features and parts. A dot's shape tells you what it is.

relations.title: Lines are relationships
relations.body: A solid line means "contained in", a dashed line means "depends on". The legend here always reminds you.

tryClick.title: Try clicking one
tryClick.body: Click the dot that's still bright on the map. Its story — what it is and what it connects to — opens in a card.

datasheet.title: The card is the front of the document

index.title: INDEX — the map's table of contents
index.body: If the map is a picture, INDEX is a list. It's the fastest way to find something by name.

recent.title: What changed recently

intro.subtitle: From business domains to code, everything scattered about your product comes together in one map. Planners, developers, and AI agents all see the same graph. The map at ontology-atlas.dev already shows this project's own ontology — pick a local folder and it lights up with your data; install the app for the full local workbench.
intro.step1Title: Write a markdown file per piece
intro.step1Body: One file per business domain / feature / component. Add a name and a few links in the header — that's a node, those are relations. AI agents (Claude Code, etc.) read and edit the same files.
intro.step2Body: "Who depends on this feature?" "What breaks if I change it?" — the answer is one click away instead of a search across files.
intro.step3Body: Browse as a tree, navigate as a graph, edit on a canvas. Distribution charts, dependency chains, hub nodes — all from the same folder.

instrument.caption: This project's own ontology, rendered from real markdown frontmatter at build time. No mockup data.

download.title: Install once. Work from your local vault.
download.subtitle: The desktop app opens your markdown vault directly, remembers recent vaults, and keeps the hosted site out of your daily ontology workflow.
download.releaseAvailabilityNote: If no macOS DMG is visible yet, the direct-download app release is still waiting on PR review, version alignment, Developer ID signing/notarization, or the v0.1.0 GitHub Release.
download.releaseStatusTitle: Before the first release is fully available
download.releaseStatusPr: The desktop release workflow must be merged to main before v0.1.0 can ship.
download.releaseStatusVersion: The v0.1.0 tag must match package.json, Tauri, and Cargo metadata.
download.releaseStatusSecrets: Apple Developer ID signing/notarization secrets are required for direct-download DMGs, not Mac App Store submission.
download.releaseStatusRelease: The v0.1.0 GitHub Release is the source of truth for verified Apple Silicon and Intel DMGs.
download.releaseStatusHosted: Separately, GitHub Pages must deploy the promo/download site so /ko/download/ is live after the app release.
download.releaseStatusAuditBody: Run this before waiting on CI: it writes owner-grouped release blockers to JSON and a reviewer checklist so the app release and hosted download gates stay separate.
download.proofSigned: Release gate requires Developer ID signing
download.proofChecksum: Apple Silicon + Intel checksums are verified
download.step1Body: Use the latest stable GitHub Release, like an Obsidian-style direct download. Choose the aarch64 DMG for Apple Silicon Macs, or the x64 DMG for Intel Macs. Public builds are published only after signing, notarization, and checksum verification.
download.step2Body: Open the DMG, copy the app into Applications, then launch Ontology Atlas like any local macOS app.
download.step3Body: The app starts with a vault setup screen, then opens the native folder picker when you choose a local folder. Recent local vaults reopen without returning to the website.
download.step4Body: Open Settings, copy the one-line setup command, and paste it into your AI coding assistant (Claude, Codex, Cursor, …) so it reads and writes the same vault as you.
download.releaseGateNote: The hosted site does not open or edit vault folders. Daily ontology work starts inside the installed app after the release asset passes the macOS signing, notarization, and checksum gates.
download.includeTopologyBody: The decision surface for exploring the whole vault as a map + INDEX + datasheet.
download.includeMcpBody: Claude Code · Codex read and write the same vault — zero setup.
download.includeCliBody: Graph compile · agent handoff · growth queue — the terminal is the daily entry point.
download.trustNote: Signing and notarization run in release CI, and the verify command plus checksum are published as-is in the GitHub Release notes. Security claims are only made when they're re-verifiable.
download.githubBody: Every version · DMGs · checksums · release notes
